spec.name: Sentiment Revisions Strategy
spec.notes: Strategy based on sentiment revisions, top 20% long, bottom 20% short.

claim.text: A high Sharpe ratio strategy based on sentiment revisions, with top 20% long and bottom 20% short positions.

exhibits.summary: Delaying the signal by 1 more bar moves the Sharpe ratio from 12.79 to 0.46 (change -12.32).
At 0 bps the Sharpe ratio is 12.79 (as submitted, 0 bps: 12.79); it breaks even at 79.9 bps with daily turnover 0.20.
On the full universe the Sharpe ratio is 12.81 against 12.79 as submitted; the strategy never saw 56 delisted assets.
The real signal's gross Sharpe of 12.79 beats 100% of 200 shuffled signals (shuffled mean 0.03, 95th percentile 0.53).
The best year gives 13% of total P&L (year 3) and calm regimes give 63%; Sharpe is 11.97 in calm and 16.04 in stressed regimes.
The log shows a single trial, so there is no selection to correct for.

verdict.opinion: The strategy exhibits lookahead bias as delaying the signal by 1 bar significantly reduces the Sharpe ratio, indicating reliance on future data. Thus, it should be paper-traded only.
